text: The receiver platform of the Arecibo Telescope in Puerto Rico collapsed into the dish after a second main cable from one of its towers failed.
Space Shuttle Endeavour launched from Kennedy Space Center on STS-61, the first servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope.
NASA's Pioneer 10 made its closest approach to Jupiter, completing the first mission to the planet.
Jeremiah Horrocks observed Venus crossing the face of the Sun from Much Hoole in England. The source gives the date as 24 November in the Julian calendar and 4 December in the Gregorian calendar.
Astronomers announced Kepler-22b, the first known transiting planet found orbiting in the habitable zone of a Sun-like star.
Venus crossed the face of the Sun in the second and last transit of the 19th century, observed by expeditions sent out by several nations.
Gerard Kuiper was born in Tuitjenhorn in the Netherlands. He discovered Miranda, a moon of Uranus, and Nereid, a moon of Neptune.
NASA's Galileo spacecraft arrived at Jupiter after gravity assist flybys of Venus and Earth.
NASA's Galileo spacecraft made its first flyby of Earth on its way to Jupiter, passing 960 kilometres above the surface.

source.title: Astronomy: Dec. 8, 1990 & 1992, Galileo flies by Earth (twice)

text: Venus passed across the Sun in the first of the two transits of the 19th century. Nations sent expeditions around the world to time it and measure the astronomical unit.
The European Space Agency launched the X-ray observatory XMM-Newton on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre.
Annie Jump Cannon was born in Dover, Delaware. She developed the Harvard scheme for classifying stars by their spectra and classified about 350,000 stars herself.
ESO released the first pictures from VISTA, its new infrared survey telescope at Paranal Observatory, after formally accepting the telescope the day before.

source.title: ESO: VISTA, pioneering new survey telescope starts work (eso0949)

text: Henrietta Swan Leavitt died in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Her period-luminosity relation for Cepheid variable stars gave astronomers a way to measure distances far beyond the reach of parallax.
Uhuru, the first satellite launched specifically for X-ray astronomy, lifted off from the San Marco platform off the coast of Kenya.

Albert Michelson and Francis Pease measured the angular diameter of Betelgeuse with an interferometer on the 2.5-metre telescope at Mount Wilson, the first such measurement for a star outside the Solar System.
J. P. M. Prentice discovered Nova Herculis 1934, now known as DQ Herculis, from Stowmarket in Suffolk.
Tycho Brahe, the Danish astronomer, was born.
NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) launched on a Delta II rocket.
Audouin Dollfus identified Janus, a small inner moon of Saturn, which received the temporary designation S/1966 S 2.
Edward Emerson Barnard was born in Nashville, Tennessee. He discovered Jupiter's moon Amalthea and photographed and catalogued the dark nebulae of the Milky Way.
The Arecibo Observatory captured radar images of the asteroid 3200 Phaethon during its flyby. The images showed a spheroidal shape and a depression near its equator.

source.title: Astronomy: Dec. 17, 2017, Arecibo images a near-Earth asteroid

text: The Hubble Space Telescope began ten days of observations of a small patch of sky, taking 342 images that became the Hubble Deep Field.
ESA's Gaia spacecraft launched on a Soyuz rocket from Kourou in French Guiana.
Carl Sagan died in Seattle at the age of 62.
Jupiter and Saturn passed within 6 arcminutes of each other in a great conjunction, the closest pairing of the two planets since 1623.
Max Wolf discovered the asteroid 323 Brucia, the first asteroid found by photography.
Giovanni Domenico Cassini discovered Rhea, a moon of Saturn, using a 10.4-metre telescope made by Giuseppe Campani.
Astronaut William Anders photographed the Earth rising over the Moon from lunar orbit during Apollo 8. The picture became known as Earthrise.
Johann Georg Palitzsch, a German farmer and amateur astronomer, sighted the returning Halley's Comet, confirming Edmond Halley's prediction.
Vera Rubin died in Princeton, New Jersey. Her measurements of how fast galaxies rotate gave strong evidence for dark matter.
The James Webb Space Telescope launched on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana.
William Herschel made the first recorded observation of NGC 2261, the nebula later known as Hubble's Variable Nebula.
Johannes Kepler was born in Weil der Stadt, Württemberg, in Germany.
Galileo observed and drew Neptune while watching Jupiter, but he took it for a fixed star.
Arthur Eddington was born in Kendal, England. He led the 1919 eclipse expedition to Príncipe that tested Einstein's theory of general relativity.
Isaac Roberts photographed the Andromeda nebula with his 20-inch reflecting telescope, and the plate showed its spiral structure.
John N. Bahcall was born in Shreveport, Louisiana. He worked for decades on the solar neutrino problem and helped develop the Hubble Space Telescope with Lyman Spitzer Jr.
Johann Elert Bode discovered the spiral galaxy M81.
